one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban shares a shortened version of his address as head of the Philippine delegation to the Asean Law Association (ALA) General Assembly and Governing Council meetings in Kuala Lumpur, Oct 17-22, graced by Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim. He announces the leadership transition of ALA Philippines: CJ Alexander G. Gesmundo, by author's strong personal request, was unanimously elected chairman effective immediately, but asked the author to carry on because he and the SC were busy with the 'Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovation' uplifting the Philippine judiciary to 'the Age of Artificial Intelligence.' By compromise, the author stays through end-2023 and Gesmundo takes over Jan 1, 2024. He names the seven sitting SC justices in the delegation (Inting, Zalameda, M. Lopez, Gaerlan, J. Lopez, Kho Jr., Singh), with appellate-court justices, retired justices, attorneys, academicians, and government lawyers totaling 50. He celebrates ALA's 40-year consensus-as-North-star tradition that has surmounted differences in national histories, customs, traditions, religions, economies, sociology, and forms of government -- including territorial and maritime disputes -- in peaceful and friendly ways. Foremost among those ways is adherence to the rule of law and abhorrence of armed, forcible, insidious, and bullying tactics, including so-called 'gray tactics' -- 'we believe in the rule of law, NOT in the rule of the mob, NOT in the rule of propaganda and falsehood, and NOT in the rule of nuclear weapons.' He quotes his Feb 26, 2015 ALA address: 'truth is eternal and limitless... humans need both justice and jobs; freedom and food; ethics and economics; peace and development; liberty and prosperity; these twin beacons must always go together; one is useless without the other.' He reports on the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity's tally -- 83 full law scholarships, 16 professorial chairs, 27 dissertation primary winners, and 10 'Esmel' fellowships for master's degrees in entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics, and business law -- and announces FLP's two 'ultimate projects': the Center for Liberty and Prosperity in Metro Manila with an immersive, interactive, AI-powered, and tech-driven Museum for Liberty and Prosperity at its core, and a multibillion-peso 'Prosperity Fund' to help the poor help themselves through private entrepreneurship. 'Before I leave this earth and enter the Great Beyond,' he hopes to complete both. He closes with a valedictory wish and prayer that consensus and the rule of law will continue reigning as the methods of attaining liberty and prosperity for the peoples of the region and the world.
